supersedes: 0.2-poc (wagashi-art-direction.json, kept unchanged for history and still selectable as v1)

policy.approved_by: the human (repo owner), after reviewing the first image of HUMAN-018
policy.change: AI-generated visuals of the wagashi themselves (and abstract materials and textures) are allowed as proposal / concept imagery. AI images of a store, its interior or exterior, staff or any people stay forbidden, as do logos, copied photos or designs and any claim that a visual is real.

goal: One professional web design comp of a one-page website for a fictional high-end wagashi shop, good enough to show in a sales demo and to implement as a real site: a header nav and three clearly separated sections (Hero, 商品・こだわり, 店舗情報) that sell the sweets themselves, not only the shop name.
source: Second Root design-library v0.3 PoC; curated by Claude from the human's review of the first mockup (2026-10-21). Concepts only, no copied site layouts or third-party photos.
theme: A contemporary high-end wagashi brand: quiet, precise and appetising. Calm kinari paper tones, sumi-black type and one muted vermilion accent; generous whitespace; the confections are the colour and the hero of the page. Modern, not a generic 和風 template (no shrine motifs, no ornamental borders, no seigaiha wallpaper).

palette.name: pale kinari
palette.use: card and info-block surfaces, alternate section band

palette.name: sumi 墨黒
palette.use: headings, body text, header, hairline rules

palette.name: muted vermilion 落ち着いた朱
palette.use: the single accent: CTA, active nav underline, small section markers; never large fills

typography.display: A refined Mincho (明朝) for the shop name, section headings and card captions; elegant, high contrast, generous letter spacing for Japanese.
typography.body: A clean Gothic (ゴシック) sans for nav, labels, information values and the disclosure; regular weight, comfortable line height.
typography.scale: Real web sizes: shop name the largest type on the page but sized to share the hero with the visual (never a poster headline that hides the sweets); section headings clearly smaller; body and info text at normal reading size.

grid.desktop: 12 columns with even gutters; content aligned to a few shared axes.
grid.max_width: About 1200 px of content centred in a 1440 px desktop page (the comp shows that page scaled down).
grid.margins: Generous outer margins and large vertical spacing between sections; whitespace is part of the luxury.

sections.label: Hero
sections.intent: Two leads in balance: the shop name 架空菓庵 and an appetising wagashi visual. Quality and appetite first.
sections.layout: Asymmetric split on the 12-col grid: a large AI concept image of a dorayaki cut in half, showing the glossy tsubu-an texture in the cross-section, on about 7 columns; the shop name in Mincho, a thin vermilion rule and the CTA on the remaining columns.

sections.label: 商品・こだわり
sections.intent: Show the seasonal jō-namagashi and the tsubu-an dorayaki as things to want. Visual, never a text-only section.
sections.layout: Section label, then a row of 2 to 3 product visual cards plus one short copy block aligned to the grid. Captions only as phrases copied verbatim from the description (季節の上生菓子, 粒あんのどら焼き) in small Mincho; a third card, if present, is the tsubu-an macro with no caption. Copy only verbatim from the description or neutral placeholder lines.

sections.label: 店舗情報
sections.intent: Precise, quiet information design that a visitor can scan in seconds.
sections.layout: Section label, then a two-column definition list (label in warm grey Gothic, value in sumi) for opening hours, closed days, address and phone, set on a pale kinari band with hairline rules; a CTA-free, tidy block. A small footer below with the shop name and the disclosure.

food_visuals.status: AI-generated concept imagery for a design proposal; never presented as photos of this shop's products.
food_visuals.lighting: Soft directional daylight from one side, gentle shadows, warm but natural colour; no harsh flash, no heavy vignette.
food_visuals.surfaces: Abstract materials only: washi paper, a pale wooden tray, an unglazed or matte ceramic plate, linen. No room, counter, shelf or shop setting behind.
food_visuals.cross_section: The hero dorayaki is cut cleanly in half: even golden-brown castella layers and a thick layer of glossy tsubu-an with visible whole azuki beans.
food_visuals.macro: One card may be a close macro of the tsubu-an texture or the soft skin of the dorayaki.
food_visuals.seasonal_motif: One card shows a seasonal jō-namagashi (for example an autumn maple or chestnut motif shaped by hand) on a small plate; delicate, matte, realistic proportions.
food_visuals.consistency: All images share one art direction: same light direction, the same muted kinari and sumi environment, similar camera height and depth of field: one consistent art direction.
food_visuals.never: No people, no hands, no faces, no staff; no store exterior, interior, signage or noren with writing; no packaging with a brand or logo; no text inside the images.

web_ui.header: A slim header bar: the shop name small at the left (as type, not a logo mark) and 2 anchor links at the right (to the two sections below the Hero).
web_ui.footer: A thin footer with the shop name in small type and the disclosure line.
web_ui.hierarchy: Clear hierarchy: header < hero (largest) > section headings > card captions > body and info values; consistent spacing that a developer could turn into CSS.

techniques.name: product-led hero
techniques.use: The wagashi image carries the appetite; the shop name carries the brand; both read at first glance.
techniques.avoid: A name so large that it covers or crowds the sweets; a text-only hero.

techniques.name: card row with air
techniques.use: Two or three equal product cards on the grid with generous gutters; captions only verbatim description phrases, or none.
techniques.avoid: Busy collages, overlapping images, carousels with arrows.

techniques.name: definition-list information
techniques.use: Label / value pairs on two columns with hairline rules; numbers and addresses set horizontally.
techniques.avoid: Vertical text for hours or addresses; icons for every row; a map screenshot.

techniques.name: one accent colour
techniques.use: Muted vermilion only for the CTA, the active nav item and tiny markers.
techniques.avoid: Large red fills, gradients, gold foil, glow.

techniques.name: implementable restraint
techniques.use: Flat colour, hairlines, real image crops and web fonts that CSS can reproduce.
techniques.avoid: Paint splashes, 3-D lettering, heavy textures over text, effects that need hand compositing.

avoid: A shop name so large that it hides the product
Over-the-top effects that are hard to implement
The generic template-like 和風 site look (shrine motifs, ornamental frames, seigaiha or asanoha wallpaper, brush splashes)
Purchase, order, reservation or online-shop UI (no cart, buy or reserve buttons)
disclosure: 架空店舗のデザイン提案｜和菓子の画像はAI生成のイメージです
hard_rules: The wagashi images are AI concept imagery for a design proposal, never photos of a real shop's products
Show the disclosure exactly: 架空店舗のデザイン提案｜和菓子の画像はAI生成のイメージです
No prices, reviews or ratings, awards, founding years or history, people or staff, and no photos or images of a store
Use only the business facts provided with this request, exactly as given; invent nothing
Placeholder test values in the facts (names containing テスト, a test station) may be left out instead of shown
No logo, emblem or crest; the shop name is set as type
Original composition; no copying of Instagram, third-party photos or other sites
No publication; the image is a design spec for a later implementation
Text in the generated image is NOT a source of truth; the later implementation takes its copy from the provided facts, never from the pixels
